lines.text: The rider from Kesting reached us at dawn. His horse fell dead at our gate. He nearly followed it.
My lord. The White came down the pass in the night. Snow like a wall. And beasts, hundreds of them. Wolves, bears, and things with no names.
The King's column was camped under our walls. We let them in. Two hundred of them and thirty of ours, all shut in the keep. And the beasts are all around it.
Thirty men hold my keep. Thirty, and two hundred southerners who can't tell snow from sugar. I ride now.
He had twenty riders with him. Twenty, against the White.
Oswin. Muster the militia. Sixty of our best, and every Skeld who'll come.
My lord. That column came here to arrest you.
Then they'll need to be alive to do it.
Kesting is three days by the road, my lord. And the road will be buried by now.
Not by the road. Through the White. The Skeld know the ice. Two days, if your lord walks in front. The snow melts where he steps.
Farmers. You're bringing farmers to my wall.
I'm bringing Greyhollow.
Lady Marrick loaded our sledges before anyone asked her. Food for eighty, for ten days, counted to the last biscuit.
Bring my sledges back, Lord Lucan. I counted those too.
I'll stay and guard your hall, Lord Lucan. Someone should.
Tamsin stayed too. To guard the guard.
Bring them all back, my lord. Every one.
I intend to.
Two days in the White at harvest time? Finally, a holiday!
I had never taken my people this far from home. With every step past our fields, I felt the threads pull, like a hundred ropes in a gale.
Ahead of us, on the mountain, Kesting's beacon was still burning. I prayed it would burn for two more days.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter fifty-three, coming soon.
